newsitem.title: USA: Lexington agrees to acquire CRIT.
newsitem.headline: Lexington agrees to acquire CRIT.

text.p: Lexington Corporate Properties Inc said Friday it had agreed to acquire Corporate Realty Income Trust I in a transaction that will be accretive to funds from operations.

In the merger, Lexington said, it will assume about $15.36 million of mortgage debt and make a payment of $18.15 million, of which at least $17.15 million will be comprised of Lexington common stock issued to CRIT stockholders.
The balance of the payment will be distributed to CRIT stockholders following payment of CRIT's expenses.
The balance would be payable in cash or shares of Lexington common stock, at the option of CRIT.

The number of shares issued by Lexington will be based on the closing price of Lexington stock during the 20 trading days preceding the fifth business day prior to the date of the CRIT stockholders' meeting.
The transaction, which is subject to approval by CRIT stockholders and certain other customary conditions, is expected to close in September, Lexington said.

CRIT's assets consist principally of three commercial real estate properties -- a 289,000-square-foot headquarters building leased to Circuit City Stores Inc in Richmond, Va.; a 148,000-square-foot industrial facility leased to Dana Corp in Gordonsville, Tenn., and a 124,000-square-foot industrial facility leased to Allegiance Healthcare Corp in Bessemer, Ala.

T. Wilson Eglin, president of Lexington, said, "This transaction will be immediately accretive to funds from operations, extend the weighted average lease term of our portfolio, and further strengthen tenant credit quality.

"We are excited to have the opportunity to grow our asset base profitably without a significant cash outlay while adding equity to our balance sheet. The transaction will also lower our ratio of debt to total market capitalization."
Lexington is a self-managed and self-administered real estate investment trust.
